newsitem.title: USA: Gay rights groups condemn Atlanta club bombing.
newsitem.headline: Gay rights groups condemn Atlanta club bombing.

text.p: Lesbian and gay rights activists on Saturday condemned the bombing of a popular gay and lesbian nightclub in Atlanta and urged the Justice Department to investigate if the bombing was a hate crime.
The FBI suspected a serial bomber might be behind the explosion, which injured five and resembled bombings at an Atlanta abortion clinic last month and at the Olympic Centennial Park last July.
The National Gay and Lesbian Task Force wrote to President Bill Clinton on Saturday pressing him to "speak out loudly" against the attack with a bomb packed with shrapnel.

"The vicious nature of this attack, as well as the similarities with the recent abortion clinic bombings, is consistent with the hate and violence stirred up by the right-wing in this country," the New York City Gay and Lesbian Anti-Violence Project said in a statement.

"Hate clearly is a possible motive in these crimes and must be investigated as such," said Elizabeth Birch, executive director of Human Rights Campaign, the nation's largest lesbian and gay political organisation.

Birch said her group planned to contact Justice Department officials. Under federal law, the Justice Department can investigate a crime as bias-motivated if it might have been driven by hate against a certain race, religion, national origin or disability. The statutes do not include sexual orientation.
According to the most recent FBI crime statistics, almost 13 percent of offenders in 1995 said their crimes were motivated by anti-gay sentiments.
